title: Policy Scripting Console: guided JSON authoring, schema-aware validation, and scenario dry-run
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement: Customers want a single Console surface to author advanced routing policies that mix region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. Many teams prefer editing JSON/policy DSL directly (for expressiveness) but need in-context guidance, realtime schema validation, and the ability to dry-run policies against representative traffic scenarios before saving or rolling out.

Goal: Ship a 'Policy Scripting Console' panel that sits alongside the visual policy editor (optional toggle). The panel provides: a guided JSON editor with contextual help, linting against the policy schema, explainable validation errors, an integrated scenario dry-run sandbox that simulates route selection for sample requests, and a preflight summary showing affected models/regions/tier impacts. The UX should make it safe for power-users while preventing common misconfigurations for non-experts.
acceptance_criteria:
- JSON editor available as a collapsible panel in Policy > Edit route.
- Editor includes schema-driven autocomplete, inline validation messages, and a single-click 'apply to visual editor' toggle.
- Dry-run can execute up to 100 synthetic requests and return the chosen region, tier, model variant, and fallback sequence.
- Dry-run results include latency and cost heuristics (estimate) and a confidence note for model variant fallbacks.
- Validation errors surface human-readable fixes and link to docs or suggested quick-fixes.
- Audit event created for 'policy scripted change' with diff view in the policy activity log.
- Unit and e2e tests cover editor, validation, dry-run API, and rollout gating behavior.
notes:
Design trade-offs: keep visual editor parity but avoid two-source-of-truth drift. We will implement a canonical policy model on the backend; the editor toggles only change the same canonical representation. Decided not to support arbitrary scripting hooks in v1 to limit security review scope and ensure predictable rollouts.

Implementation approach: 1) reuse JSON schema used by Backend Policy Service for editor autocomplete and validation; 2) build dry-run simulator service that leverages existing routing heuristics and sample traffic generator; 3) expose a light-weight cost/latency estimator (rules-based) rather than full offline perf simulation.

Risk: users could create policies that route to low-capacity tiers—we will add preflight warnings and soft-block on policies that exceed known capacity constraints.

Open question: should we allow per-customer sample traffic upload for more representative dry-runs? PM leaning: deferred to v2 due to storage/PII concerns.
comments: 2025-02-11 - AJ (Eng): POC for schema-based autocomplete completed. Basic linting hooks in Monaco editor work end-to-end.
2025-02-13 - Ruth (PM): Design critique with Design + Eng. Agreement to surface cost estimates as ranges, not exact numbers. Action: DES to adjust microcopy explaining estimate fidelity.
2025-02-17 - Marco (Design): Figma mock for editor panel uploaded: https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/policy-scripting-console. See frames 'editor-state' and 'dryrun-results'.
2025-02-19 - Eng (SRE): Flagged potential perf impact of running simultaneous dry-runs for large customers. Proposal: queue dry-runs with priority and rate-limit per org.
2025-02-21 - Aisha (PM): Updated acceptance criteria to cap synthetic dry-run batch at 100 requests per run and add cost/latency heuristics.
2025-02-24 - Ruth (PM): PR opened for backend dry-run API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9321. Requesting design review for results UI.
2025-02-25 - DES (Design): UX microcopy updates pushed. Noted need for clearer error copy when schema version mismatches occur; added a migration hint in the editor top bar.
recommendation: Ship editor + dry-run as opt-in for early adopters. Monitor dry-run usage, track top validation errors, and iterate microcopy and quick-fixes in the next cycle. Plan v2 to add customer-supplied traffic and richer cost modeling.
post_release_actions:
- Collect top 20 validation failures and prioritize schema/hints fixes.
- Run an internal pilot with three customers to validate dry-run fidelity and UI clarity.
- Follow-up ticket to add policy diff review flow for canary rollouts (PM-26015).
